constraint_decided_it: P46 is composed of (E18->E18) scope note: 'This property does not specify when and for how long a component element resided in the respective whole. If a component is not part of a whole from the beginning of existence or until the end of existence of the whole, the classes E79 Part Addition and E90 [sic, E80] Part Removal can be used to document when a component became part of a particular whole and/or when it stopped being a part of it.' B closes by offering P46 to 'record the before/after part-whole state (engine composed of old beam vs. composed of new beam)', which is the one use P46 explicitly disclaims - asserting both beams via P46 is timeless and would state the engine has two beams at once. A proposes no property outside its declared domain/range and makes no claim its cited source does not carry.
better_modelling: Both reach what the CRM prescribes: the engine as one continuing E22 with a single 1876 E12 Production (P108, range E24, satisfied by E22); 1932 as E80 Part Removal (P112 diminished -> engine, P113 removed -> cast-iron beam) plus E79 Part Addition (P110 augmented -> engine, P111 added -> steel beam), all E18-ranged and all under P31 has modified, with a separate E12 Production for the steel beam by the second firm. Neither cited the clause that actually settles the question's 'avoid a separately produced beam' framing: E79's scope note requires that 'Both the E18 Physical Thing being augmented and the E18 Physical Thing that is being added are treated as separate identifiable wholes prior to the instance of E79 Part Addition' - so the avoidance the trust asks about is not available under E79. E80's converse clause (a part with no discernible identity before removal is modelled as E80 and E12 together) is not triggered here, since the 1876 beam was already identifiable; neither answer checked it.
reasoning: Both answers converge on the same prescribed modelling and both correctly reject E81 Transformation on E11's own wording ('results in the destruction of one or more objects and the simultaneous production of others ... the new items have separate identities'), verified verbatim in E11's scope note; both correctly note P108, P110 and P112 are siblings under P31 has modified, verified in the declarations. Every quotation checks out: A's two t1170 quotes and B's longer form of the same Doerr sentence are all FOUND in t1170 message [10], and B's Issue 221 gloss matches the register outcome 'Because there is no assumption that the part removed exist before and after, the issue is not accepted' with t0056 correctly described as the 2002 Part Addition/Removal proposal. The separation is B's added P46 recommendation, which the property's own scope note excludes for exactly this temporal use and redirects to E79/E80 - the very classes B already proposed. A's defects are rhetorical rather than ontological (P111 added is itself a subproperty of P16, so framing 'P16' as the rejected alternative is imprecise, and subclass membership under E11 does not by itself preclude a second P108), so it takes correct while B takes suboptimal.
